## Comparison (~4 GB RAM, US region)

| Provider | Plan (~4 GB) | Monthly price | Included storage | Backup retention | PITR | Free tier |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Neon** | Launch, 1 CU (4 GB) | about $77 if always on (1 CU × 730 h × $0.106). It scales to zero, so it can cost less. | None. $0.35/GB-month, usage-based. | History window up to 7 days (Scale: 30) | In the history window. Instant restore storage is billed at $0.20/GB-month. | Yes, permanent: 100 CU-hours, 1 GB per project, 6-hour restore window |
| **Supabase** | Pro + Medium compute | $25 plan + $60 compute = **$85**. The Pro plan may include a compute credit that I didn't check. | 8 GB, then $0.125/GB | 7 days | **Extra:** $100/month per 7 days | Yes. 500 MB, 2 projects, pauses after 1 week idle, no backups. |
| **Render** | Pro-4GB (third-party figure) | about $97, **unverified** | about 50 GB, **unverified**. Extra storage is $0.30/GB. | Unverified | Render's docs say paid databases get PITR. A third-party blog says the window depends on workspace plan (3 days Hobby, 7 days Pro and Scale). Unverified. | Free instances exist, but I didn't confirm the terms |
| **Railway** | No managed Postgres plan. You self-run Postgres on usage billing. | 4 GB RAM ≈ $40 + CPU + volume. Plus the $5 Hobby or $20 Pro plan fee. | Volume at $0.15/GB-month | Not documented on the pricing page | Not documented | Trial with $5 credit for 30 days, then a $1/month Free plan capped at 0.5 GB |
| **Fly.io** | **No 4 GB tier.** Starter is 2 GB and Launch is 8 GB. | Starter **$72**, Launch **$282** | None. $0.28/GB, usage-based. | Not found | Marketing says it's available. One third-party source says it's a paid add-on. Unconfirmed. | No |
| **DigitalOcean** | Standard, 4 GiB / 2 vCPU | **$60.90** | The page lists 60–120 GiB at $0.215/GiB. It's unclear whether any is included in the price. | 7 days (docs) | Included, per docs and marketing. A third-party source disagrees. | No. A $5 credit that expires after 90 days. |
| **Aiven** | Startup-4 | from **$75** | 80 GB | 2 days (Business: 14 days, from $180) | The page lists it as a feature but doesn't say per plan. I couldn't confirm it. | Yes. Free (1 GB RAM) and Developer ($5), but no choice of region. |
| **Crunchy Bridge** | Hobby-4 or Standard-4 | **$70** | None. $0.10/GB. | Not stated. Extended backups are an optional add-on. | **Included** (continuous WAL) | No. The cheapest plan is $9–10/month. |
| **Timescale (Tiger)** | Performance plan | Not published. The plan starts at $30/month. | Usage-billed | PITR up to 3 days (Scale: 14) | Included, up to the retention above | No permanent tier. 30-day trial. |
| **AWS RDS** | db.t4g.medium (4 GiB), Single-AZ | about **$47** compute (about $0.065/h, third-party aggregator) | None. You pick the EBS size. I didn't confirm the gp3 price. | Not confirmed. I believe the default is 7 days, up to 35. | I believe it's included by default. Not confirmed. | 12-month trial: 750 h, 20 GB, 20 GB backup |

## Where I used a calculator or formula
- **Neon:** I computed the figure from the per-CU-hour rate.
- **Supabase:** I summed the plan and compute add-on.
- **Railway:** I estimated from per-GB rates, because it has no fixed plan.
- **Timescale (Tiger):** Billing is hourly per CPU. The page gives a formula and an in-console forecast, but no rate for a 4 GB size.
- **AWS RDS:** The official instance-price tables didn't load. The figure comes from a third-party aggregator, and AWS's own calculator would be the authoritative source.

## Caveats
- **Render, Railway, Fly.io and Timescale (Tiger):** Check these on the vendors' own sites before you decide.
- **Aiven:** A Startup plan with 2 days of backups may not suit a production workload.
- **High availability:** I haven't compared it. It's included on Fly.io, a separate tier on Aiven, and extra on RDS (Multi-AZ).
- **Cheapest on the numbers I have:** RDS (about $47 plus storage), then DigitalOcean ($60.90), then Crunchy Bridge ($70 plus storage). That ranking leaves out storage and the unverified cells.

Sources: [Neon pricing](https://neon.com/pricing), [Supabase pricing](https://supabase.com/pricing), [Railway pricing](https://railway.com/pricing), [Fly.io Managed Postgres docs](https://docs.fly.io/mpg), [DigitalOcean managed databases pricing](https://www.digitalocean.com/pricing/managed-databases), [DigitalOcean backup restore docs](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/databases/postgresql/how-to/restore-from-backups), [Aiven pricing](https://aiven.io/pricing?product=pg), [Crunchy Data pricing](https://www.crunchydata.com/pricing), [Crunchy extended backups](https://www.crunchydata.com/blog/extended-backups-for-crunchy-bridge), [Tiger Data pricing](https://www.tigerdata.com/pricing), [AWS RDS PostgreSQL pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/rds/postgresql/pricing/), [Vantage db.t4g.medium](https://instances.vantage.sh/aws/rds/db.t4g.medium), [Render flexible plans](https://render.com/docs/postgresql-refresh), [Kuberns Render pricing (third-party)](https://kuberns.com/blogs/render-postgres-pricing-setup-limits/)
